name: Runic

historicalPeriod.text: Use in various forms covers a period from the first century to the nineteenth century.

geographicDistribution.text: Used in the German, Scandinavian, and Anglo-Saxon areas.

directionality.text: Modern scholarly literature writes Runic from left to right. This describes modern practice, not every historical inscription.

characteristics.text: Has a distinct angular appearance, owing to carving in stone and wood.
Named the futhark after its first six letters. The older futhark had 24 runes, and the simplified younger futhark had 16.

relationships.text: The shapes of most runes can be related to a Latin capital letter, and the most conspicuous difference is letter order.

referenceCharacters.name: RUNIC LETTER FEHU FEOH FE F
RUNIC LETTER RAIDO RAD REID R

limitations: Modern writing direction is not evidence for the direction of a given inscription.
Elder and younger forms differ, and a single reference glyph cannot show this.
